title: Heavenly Dao Chessboard
next_chapter_hook: Mo Xiansheng's form grew increasingly faint in the golden light, yet before vanishing completely, he left Chen Ji with one final sentence that sent a bone-deep chill through his entire being: 'The chess game has seventy-two moves remaining, but you... may not even survive one move.' Chen Ji gripped the Tianji Record Fragment, feeling its faint pulse, and for the first time, he sensed the chessboard of destiny pressing down upon him.

text.content: Upon the fragment, golden light cascaded down like a waterfall, enveloping Chen Ji entirely. He felt his vision blur, and his consciousness was forcibly pulled into an endless void. All around was ink-black darkness, yet beneath his feet, a vast and boundless chessboard faintly emerged. On the board, dense and numerous chess pieces dotted the space like stars, each piece emanating a faint glow—some bright as the scorching sun, others dim as fireflies. Mo Xiansheng's figure floated above the chessboard, his aged face now radiating an otherworldly, dignified authority.

'This is the Heavenly Dao Chessboard.' Mo Xiansheng's voice echoed through the void. 'What you believed to be destiny is merely a chess game laid out by higher existences. What you thought was fortune was merely the residual glance of a chess player placing a piece. What you considered rebellion is nothing but futile struggle along a predetermined path.' Chen Ji gazed at the boundless chessboard beneath his feet, an indescribable chill rising in his heart. Those flickering chess pieces, each representing a life, a soul—and he was one of them.

dialogue.content: 'Do you see clearly now?' Mo Xiansheng waved his hand, and suddenly dozens of lights blazed upon the chessboard, one of which was赫然located precisely beneath Chen Ji's feet. 'That piece there is you.' Chen Ji lowered his head to see the piece beneath his feet, pitch-black as ink, forming a stark contrast with the surrounding bright glow. Mo Xiansheng coldly smiled: 'You think this is degradation? No, this is the mark chosen for you by the Tianji Record. Black means you are the last piece yet to be placed in this chess game.'

text.content: Chen Ji's heart sank violently. He gazed at the chessboard beneath him, watching the bright and dim pieces intertwining, and vaguely understood something. Mo Xiansheng pointed to an obvious gap at the edge of the chessboard: 'Do you see it? There's a piece missing there.' Chen Ji looked intently and indeed, at the southeastern corner of the chessboard, there was a blank space, and the surrounding pieces all orbited around that emptiness, as if something should have existed there but was deliberately removed. 'In ancient times, there was a prophecy.' Mo Xiansheng's voice grew lower. 'That prophet should have placed a piece there, but midway, he chose self-destruction, leaving a gap that could never be filled.'

dialogue.content: 'And you, Chen Ji.' Mo Xiansheng turned around, his aged gaze carrying a complex emotion. 'You are the seed cultivated to fill that gap.' Chen Ji abruptly raised his head, his pupils contracting. Cultivated? He had been a servant in the Tianqing Sect since childhood, enduring endless bullying, treated as waste, and even his missing sister had been taken by the Holy Sect for reasons he still knew nothing about. Were all these arranged? 'From the moment you were born, the Tianji Record had already chosen your bloodline.' Mo Xiansheng's voice was icy cold. 'Your parents did not die in an accident—they were cleansed by Heavenly Dao, because their existence would interfere with the cultivation of you, this chess piece.'

text.content: Chen Ji felt as if a massive boulder was crushing his chest, almost suffocating him. His hands unconsciously clenched tightly, his knuckles whitening from force. The rage at being treated as a chess piece, the resentment toward fate's unfairness, and that bone-deep chill intertwined, almost tearing him apart. Yet his expression remained calm—that restraint honed through countless moments between life and death was now his only armor. Mo Xiansheng seemed quite satisfied with his reaction and continued: 'You think obtaining the Tianji Record was a lucky coincidence? No, the Fragment needs a vessel, and the bloodline within you happens to be capable of bearing it. The so-called inheritance is merely making you a more suitable chess piece.'

Chen Ji slowly raised his head, his gaze piercing through the void to land on that vast chessboard above. His voice was very soft, so soft that almost no emotion could be discerned: 'So, everything I've done over these years—enduring, strategizing, scheming—in the eyes of Heavenly Dao, was merely a chess piece moving on its own?' 'Exactly.' Mo Xiansheng nodded. 'You think your strategies are flawless? Laughable. Every time you use the Tianji Record, you are under Heavenly Dao's observation. The future you see is the future you are permitted to see; the chess game you arrange is the chess game you are confined within.' Chen Ji closed his eyes and took a deep breath. When he opened them again, that suppressed fury had vanished, replaced by a chilling calm.

dialogue.content: 'Then let me ask.' Chen Ji's voice was terrifyingly calm. 'Since the Heavenly Dao Chessboard has been set up, what are you? You keep calling me a chess piece, but what role do you play in this chess game?' Mo Xiansheng's movement paused slightly. After a moment, he bitterly smiled: 'Good question. I am merely a wisp of remnant soul, the final backup left by Chen Xuan before his fall. My existence itself is to reveal the truth to you at the appropriate moment—and this is also part of being a chess piece.' His voice carried a hint of self-mockery. 'Even my self-importance was calculated within the chess game.'

text.content: Chen Ji gazed at Mo Xiansheng's aged face, and suddenly a strange feeling surged within him. This being who claimed to be his master's remnant soul now appeared even more lonely than himself. He had slept within this chess game for hundreds of years, and upon waking, the first thing he did was reveal the truth to Chen Ji—yet this truth itself was merely part of the chess game. This absurd sense of destiny made Chen Ji almost want to laugh aloud. Yet he ultimately did not laugh. He simply stood quietly in the void, gazing at the chessboard beneath his feet, silent for a long while.

choice.prompt: Mo Xiansheng had revealed the truth, but Chen Ji must make a choice: to accept his fate as a chess piece, or to seek a way to break the game?

choices.description: Since the Heavenly Dao Chessboard is so vast, confronting it recklessly would be like an egg striking a rock. Better to continue playing the role of a chess piece and secretly accumulate power to break the game.
choices.visible_cost: Consuming time to let the chess game continue operating
choices.visible_reward: Gaining more intelligence about how the chess game operates
choices.risk_hint: Potentially falling deeper into the chess game's traps

dialogue.content: Chen Ji slowly closed his eyes, pressing all his fury and unwillingness into the depths of his heart. When he opened them again, that chilling calm had returned. 'Since I am a chess piece, then I shall first do what a chess piece should do.' His voice was terrifyingly calm. 'At least until I find a flaw.' Mo Xiansheng gazed at him, a flash of approval flickering in his aged eyes: 'Good. You are more suited to this role than I imagined.'

'However.' Chen Ji suddenly shifted his tone. 'Since the chess game has been laid bare, I would like to ask—on this chessboard, besides me, what other key pieces are there?' Mo Xiansheng was slightly stunned, then burst into laughter: 'Excellent! Excellent! Excellent! After being told the truth, the first thing is not anger, not despair, but to continue gathering intelligence—Chen Xuan did not misjudge you.' He tapped the chessboard, and several lights illuminated: 'Watch carefully. These are the key pieces in the chess game.'

choices.text: Borrowing Momentum to Break the Game
choices.description: Since Heavenly Dao has set up this chessboard, it must have intentions. Since I am a key chess piece, then I shall use myself as a bargaining chip, and use the hands of various forces to disrupt the chess game.
choices.visible_cost: May expose ambitions and bring deadly danger
choices.visible_reward: Gaining key intelligence to oppose Heavenly Dao
choices.risk_hint: Once failed, will become the priority target for Heavenly Dao's elimination

dialogue.content: A cold sneer suddenly curled at the corner of Chen Ji's mouth: 'Since Heavenly Dao needs this chess piece of mine, then this piece shall see what price it is actually worth.' Mo Xiansheng's brow furrowed: 'What do you mean?' Chen Ji raised his head, his gaze sharp as a blade: 'In this chess game, there is not only Heavenly Dao as a chess player, right? Those sects that layout the world, the Holy Sect, even the Eye of Heavenly Dao you mentioned—they are not of one mind, are they?'

Mr. Mo's expression changed. Gazing at Chen Ji, the aged eyes in his face revealed genuine surprise for the first time: "You actually thought this through?" Chen Ji replied coolly: "Since this is a chess game, there must be chess players. Between chess players, there must be manipulation. I don't need to defeat the Heavenly Dao, I just need to become a variable between them—one that they all want to recruit, yet none dare to easily use." Mr. Mo remained silent for a long while before finally sighing: "Chen Xuan, oh Chen Xuan, what did you see a thousand years ago to choose this child?"

choices.description: Since the Tianji Record is a piece placed by the Heavenly Dao, what is its true origin? Tracing back to its initial source might reveal a way to disrupt the cosmic chess game.
choices.visible_cost: Risk falling into deeper fate entanglements
choices.visible_reward: Obtain crucial information for opposing the Heavenly Dao
choices.risk_hint: Tracing the origin may come with unpredictable costs

dialogue.content: Chen Ji didn't rush to take a stance. Instead, he asked a crucial question: "Where does the Tianji Record come from?" Mr. Mo's movement suddenly froze. Chen Ji continued: "You said the Tianji Record is a piece placed by the Heavenly Dao, then when did the Heavenly Dao itself begin setting up this chess game?" Mr. Mo fell silent for a long time, the atmosphere in the Void becoming extraordinarily heavy. Finally, he spoke, his voice carrying an unusual hint of wariness: "This question... even I don't know the answer. But I can tell you, the origin of the Tianji Record is even older than the Heavenly Dao chess game itself."

text.content: A chill ran through Chen Ji's heart. Older than the Heavenly Dao chess game? That meant the Tianji Record's origins were far more complex than he had imagined. Mr. Mo seemed to sense his confusion and continued: "There are rumors that the Tianji Record was originally not an object of the Heavenly Dao, but came from an era that has long been extinguished. That era's civilization has completely vanished from the river of history—the Heavenly Dao is merely a remnant of that civilization." Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. This information was too shocking, leaving him momentarily unable to digest it. If the Heavenly Dao wasn't the most ancient existence, then who was the true mastermind?

Mr. Mo raised his hand and tapped the chessboard. Several rays of light suddenly blazed forth. Chen Ji looked closely to see those lights in different colors—gold, crimson, azure, black, and white—interwoven together like a complex network of relationships. "These are the key pieces in the chess game," Mr. Mo's voice was low. "Gold represents the Eye of the Heavenly Dao, symbolizing the chess player; crimson represents the three major sects, they are the main forces in the game; azure represents the Tianqing Sect, you are an underestimated dark piece among them; black represents the Demonic Holy Sect, their purpose remains an enigma to this day; white represents..." His voice paused. "White represents your missing sister for many years—Chen Nian."

dialogue.content: Chen Ji's heart tightened sharply. "Nian Nian?" His voice carried obvious fluctuation for the first time. "What role does she play in the chess game?" Mr. Mo gazed deeply at him: "Do you still not understand why the Eye of the Heavenly Dao took her away?" Chen Ji fell silent. Of course he understood. Chen Nian was his weakness; the Heavenly Dao taking her was meant to restrain him through her. But the deeper meaning in Mr. Mo's words seemed to go beyond that. "She is the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key'," Mr. Mo said slowly. "The so-called lock key can open or close the Heavenly Dao chess game. The fate of ordinary people, the Heavenly Dao can freely alter; but if a variable appears, the Heavenly Dao needs the lock key to make corrections."

text.content: Chen Ji finally understood. The Heavenly Dao cultivated him into a piece to fill the gaps in the chess game; while taking Chen Nian away was to completely lock him as a piece when necessary. Chen Nian's existence was like a counterweight on a scale—when Chen Ji the piece showed enough value, the Heavenly Dao would use Chen Nian to restrain him; when Chen Ji the piece lost control, the Heavenly Dao would use Chen Nian to destroy him. In either case, Chen Nian was merely a tool in the Heavenly Dao's hands. Thinking of this, an overwhelming killing intent surged in Chen Ji's heart. But that killing intent only flashed briefly before he forcibly suppressed it. It wasn't time yet.

Mr. Mo gazed at the fleeting killing intent in Chen Ji's eyes, and an expression of relief actually appeared on his aged face. "Good." He said, "Anger is fine, but don't let it blind your eyes. In the chess game, anger is the most useless emotion—it only exposes your weaknesses." Chen Ji took a deep breath and slowly calmed the turmoil in his heart. When he raised his head again, his gaze had returned to its usual calmness. "I understand." He said, "I'll find a way regarding Nian Nian's matter. But now, I need to know more—when will the chess game reach its final phase? And what will happen after the final phase?"

choice.prompt: Mr. Mo is about to reveal the secret of the chess game's endgame, and Chen Ji must decide what posture to adopt when facing this truth.

choices.description: The more one faces earth-shaking truths, the more one must remain calm. Rationally analyze the operating patterns of the chess game, seeking flaws within it.
choices.risk_hint: Excessive rationality may overlook emotional factors

dialogue.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes, rapidly organizing the known information in his mind. The Heavenly Dao chess game, the incomplete Tianji Record, the chosen bloodline, the missing sister, the approaching endgame... these fragments gradually assembled into a complete picture in his mind. When he opened his eyes again, a hint of understanding flickered in his gaze: "I understand now. The so-called endgame is not the end of a war, but the convergence of the chess game. The Heavenly Dao needs me this piece to fill the gap, but that doesn't mean it will let me live until that moment."

Mr. Mo nodded: "You're very clever. The Heavenly Dao cultivated you as a piece, naturally it will discard you at the appropriate time. Just like Chen Xuan—he was once an existence more brilliant than me, yet in the end, he was merely a piece sacrificed in the chess game." Chen Ji did not speak. He quietly gazed at the chessboard at his feet, at those flickering pieces, while his mind rapidly calculated. There were still seventy-two moves until the endgame, but his time was running out. He had to find the possibility of a comeback before being discarded.

choices.description: There are不止 (more than) the Heavenly Dao as a single force in the chess game—the three major sects, the Demonic Holy Sect, and even other chosen pieces, could become objects of cooperation.
choices.risk_hint: Cooperation partners may harbor ulterior motives

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji suddenly thought of something: 'The Holy Sect's Saintess Ye Qing from the Demonic Path—is she also a chess piece?' Mo Xiansheng slightly startled, then nodded: 'She is a piece being used. The Holy Sect wants to control the Demonic Path through her, and the Heavenly Dao also wants her to disrupt the chess game. But she herself seems to have noticed something.' A faint smile curved Chen Ji's lips. He remembered that deal with Ye Qing, remembered her shock when she saw the prophecy. If he could make Ye Qing completely side with him..."

"Mo Xiansheng seemed to read his thoughts, shaking his head: 'Ye Qing can be used, but cannot be fully trusted. Her Demonic Path mist can conceal the aura of the Tianji Record—that is her greatest value. But the restriction the Holy Sect placed on her still exists. Once she becomes your ally, that restriction will become her death warrant.' Chen Ji's gaze slightly hardened. This meant that unless the restriction on Ye Qing could be removed, she could never become a true ally. And the method to remove the restriction... there was probably only one path: a complete break with the Holy Sect."

choices.description: "Since all truths have been revealed, why not directly question Mo Xiansheng—as Chen Xuan's leftover trump card, what else hasn't he said?"
choices.risk_hint: "Mo Xiansheng may be holding something back"

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji suddenly stepped forward,直视 Mo Xiansheng's eyes: 'You said you're Chen Xuan's leftover trump card, then tell me—what did Chen Xuan see back then that made him choose self-destruction and leave this unfillable gap?' Mo Xiansheng's expression suddenly froze. Chen Ji pressed on: 'An inheritor chosen by the Heavenly Dao, a being at the pinnacle of power, why would he destroy everything with his own hands? Unless—he saw an ending even more terrifying than becoming a chess piece.'"

"Mo Xiansheng fell silent. After a long while, his voice actually carried a tremor: 'You really are... as clever as Chen Xiansheng.' He raised his head, and the ancient eyes revealed a deep fear, 'Chen Xiansheng saw the truth of the endgame—when a chess piece fills the gap, that is the moment the Chess Player harvests. You think filling the gap grants power? No, that means offering all fates, all karma, all possibilities... to the Eye of Heavenly Dao. And Chen Xiansheng was unwilling to become that sacrifice.' Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. Sacrifice. So that was it. The inheritor of the Tianji Record was a sacrifice from the very beginning."

text.content: "Chen Ji stood in the Void, feeling the tide of coldness in his heart. So that was it. He thought he was a cultivated chess piece, but from the start, he was the chosen sacrifice. Every inheritance of the Tianji Record was preparing for the final offering. And Chen Xiansheng—that ancestor he never met—chose self-destruction to end this sacrifice. But he failed. Or rather, the Heavenly Dao was prepared. Chen Xiansheng's death didn't end the chess game; instead, it left that gap forever on the board, waiting for the next sacrifice. And he, Chen Ji, was that chosen sacrifice."

dialogue.content: "'So you understand now?' Mo Xiansheng's voice carried a hint of desolation, 'You ask me why I must tell you these things? Because I have no choice. Before Chen Xiansheng fell, he placed his final hope on you—he believed you could find another path. But I must also tell you, this path... has almost no possibility of success.' Chen Ji静静地望着他，没有说话。Mo Xiansheng continued: 'Chen Xiansheng was already at the half-step Heavenly Dao level back then, and even he couldn't find a way out. As a mere Foundation Building cultivator, what makes you think...' He didn't finish, because Chen Ji suddenly smiled."

text.content: "Chen Ji's smile was faint, yet carried an chilling coldness. 'A half-step Heavenly Dao level Chen Xiansheng couldn't find a way out doesn't mean I can't either.' His voice was terrifyingly calm, 'Because he was alone. And I... have attachments, have weaknesses, have people I want to protect. These things you see as weaknesses are precisely what allows me to break the chess game.' Mo Xiansheng was stunned. Chen Ji continued: 'The Heavenly Dao wants to use Chen Nian to restrain me—that's its calculation. But it forgot one thing—precisely because Chen Nian is my weakness, she is also my greatest variable. The Heavenly Dao cannot predict how far I would go for Chen Nian, because it itself... has never truly understood 'attachment'.'"

choice.prompt: "Chen Ji had found the key to breaking the chess game—not power, but bonds. Now he needed to decide his next move."

choices.description: "Since Chen Nian is the key variable, first rescue her. With Chen Nian, the Heavenly Dao can no longer use her to restrain me."
choices.visible_cost: "May expose one's intentions, attracting the Heavenly Dao's vigilance"
choices.visible_reward: "Gain a true variable, breaking the chess game balance"
choices.risk_hint: "The Holy Sect's strength is unfathomable, acting rashly may cost one's life"

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji's gaze became resolute: 'Niannian... I will definitely rescue her.' Mo Xiansheng looked at him, ancient eyes flashing a complex expression: 'Do you know what this means? The reason the Holy Sect made Chen Nian the 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key' is because her existence itself resonates with the Heavenly Dao's chess game. Rescuing her means directly playing chess against the Heavenly Dao—a game you almost have no chance of winning.' Chen Ji didn't retreat: 'That still beats being a well-behaved sacrificial lamb waiting to die.'"

text.content: "Mo Xiansheng was silent for a long time, finally letting out a long sigh: 'Fine. Since you've made your decision, I'll tell you a secret—the place where Chen Nian is imprisoned is beneath the Forbidden Grounds of Tianqing Sect. That is where the ancient prophets fell, and also the starting point of the Heavenly Dao's chess game. If you truly want to save her... there may lie all the answers you need.' Chen Ji slightly nodded. Forbidden Grounds. The Forbidden Grounds of Tianqing Sect. So all the answers were hidden in the place most familiar to him. This irony, he would remember."

choices.description: "The incompleteness of the Tianji Record is both a limitation and a protection. Instead of risking rescuing Chen Nian, first complete the Tianji Record and master more capital for breaking the game."
choices.visible_cost: "Need to search for scattered fragments of the Tianji Record"
choices.risk_hint: "The more complete the Tianji Record, the stronger the Heavenly Fate backlash may become"

dialogue.content: After a moment of contemplation, Chen Ji spoke: "The Tianji Record is incomplete, but the power it contains is still considerable. Rather than act recklessly, why not first complete the fragments?" Mo Xiansheng shook his head: "Completing the Tianji Record is no easy task. The other fragments are scattered everywhere—some in the hands of the three major sects, some controlled by the Holy Sect of the Demonic Path, and some have even fallen into the Eye of Heavenly Mandate's scheme." A cold smile curved Chen Ji's lips: "Isn't that perfect? The process of recovering the fragments is itself the process of disrupting the chess game."

Mo Xiansheng gazed at Chen Ji, and a faint smile actually appeared on his aged features: "Clever strategy. Using the recovery of fragments as a pretext to disrupt the chess game. Let Heavenly Mandate, the major sects, and the Holy Sect suspect each other, while you... seek the opportunity to break the situation in the chaos." He paused, then added: "But I must remind you, every time the Tianji Record becomes more complete, the backlash of Heavenly Fate grows stronger. You have already consumed considerable Heavenly Fate Value. If you continue using the complete Tianji Record... I'm afraid you won't reach the final outcome before being destroyed by Heavenly Fate's backlash."

choices.description: Su Qingyao, the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow of the Tianqing Sect, is the only person who has noticed his abnormality. Rather than continuing to hide, it would be better to draw her into the chess game.
choices.risk_hint: Su Qingyao's position is sensitive and involves the upper echelons of the Tianqing Sect

dialogue.content: Chen Ji suddenly thought of another person—Su Qingyao. That Inner Disciple Senior Fellow who always looked at him with scrutinizing eyes, that woman who had come infinitely close to the truth three times yet was cleverly deflected by him. "Su Qingyao..." Chen Ji murmured, "She is a disciple of the Tianqing Sect's former Sect Master Ling Yuan. If I can draw her into the chess game, perhaps I can break the Tianqing Sect's situation from within." Mo Xiansheng nodded: "Su Qingyao is indeed a variable. Her loyalty to the Tianqing Sect is not as simple as it appears, and... she seems to have an obsession with you that transcends ordinary fellow disciples."

Chen Ji recalled the small moments he had spent with Su Qingyao. Her three investigations—each time he had deflected her in different ways, yet she had never given up her suspicion. Looking back now, perhaps her persistence was not merely out of a sense of justice, but possibly... a kind of intuition. "She's a promising talent," Chen Ji said softly. "If I can cultivate her into a true ally, she might become the key to turning the tide at a critical moment." Mo Xiansheng fell silent for a moment, then finally said: "This is your choice. But remember, once you draw her into the chess game, she can no longer stay out of it. Are you certain... you want her to take this risk?"

text.content: Mo Xiansheng's form began to grow illusory, the remnant soul power that sustained his existence was rapidly dissipating. "Time... is running out." His voice became fleeting, "What I have revealed to you is enough. The remaining path... you must walk it yourself." Chen Ji gazed at his gradually fading form, and a complex emotion surged in his heart. This old man had once been his nominal master, yet also the one who pushed him deeper into the chess game. But regardless, he had given Chen Ji the most precious thing—the right to choose.

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji." Mo Xiansheng's voice grew increasingly faint, "Remember... in the chess game, the greatest variable... is never power, but the human heart. Heaven's Mandate calculated everything, yet it cannot calculate... the bonds and obsessions in the human heart. That is its only blind spot... and your only hope..." As the words fell, Mo Xiansheng's form completely scattered into the Void. Chen Ji stood alone on the Heavenly Mandate Chessboard, gazing at those flickering chess pieces beneath his feet, long without speaking. Bonds and obsessions? He lowered his head, looking at his tightly clenched fist. Yes. He had Nian Nian as a weakness, but Nian Nian was also his greatest strength. To protect her, he was willing to make enemies of the entire Heavenly Mandate. And this willingness was the variable that the Heavenly Mandate could never calculate.

text.content: The golden light dissipated, and Chen Ji's consciousness returned to reality. He found himself still kneeling before the fragment, Mo Xiansheng in front of him had completely vanished, leaving only an empty stone chamber. But in his heart, great waves were churning. Heavenly Mandate Chess Game, Fate Chessboard, chosen sacrifice... all of this echoed in his mind. However, Chen Ji did not fall into fear or despair. Instead, a faint smile curved his lips. "The Heavenly Mandate wants to use me as a sacrifice?" he murmured softly, his voice carrying a chilling coldness that sent shivers down the spine, "Then let's see... whether it has outsmarted me, or whether I will devour it."

Chen Ji rose to his feet and tucked the fragment into his chest. He knew that from this moment on, his fate had fundamentally changed. The Heavenly Mandate Chess Game still had seventy-two moves remaining, but he did not have seventy-two moves of time—he had to find a way to break the situation in a shorter time. Rescuing Nian Nian, completing the Tianji Record, contacting allies... every step was a dangerous move, every step required meticulous calculation. But he had no retreat and no choice. Walking out of the stone chamber, the night wind brushed his face, carrying a chill. Chen Ji raised his head toward the漆黑的夜空, his smile deepening. The Heavenly Mandate had set up a chess game, wanting to use him as a sacrifice? Very well. Then Chen Ji would, within this chess game, play a game that would overturn heaven and earth.
